summary: For a sufficiently generic semisimple two-dimensional residual representation over an unramified p-adic field, this roadmap computes framed potentially crystalline deformation rings for one tame inertial type and for the types containing a fixed Serre weight. Rank-two gauge charts and effective monodromy approximation give Hodge-labelled components, reduced special fibres and an integral component-intersection identity needed in patching. The two Hodge profiles are (3,0) and (2,1); the construction therefore extends beyond potentially Barsotti–Tate weights.

nodes.title: Tame inertial types
nodes.statement: For s∈(S₂)^f and μ∈(Z²)^f, let sτ=s₀s_{f−1}⋯s₁, r=ord(sτ), f′=rf, e′=p^{f′}−1. Put α′_j=(s₁⁻¹⋯s_j⁻¹)(μ_j+η), η=(1,0), with periodic indices modulo f and α′_{j+kf}=sτ^{−k}α′_j. Set a′^(j)=Σ_{i=0}^{f′−1}p^i α′_{−j+i}. The characteristic-zero inertial type τ(s,μ+η) is the sum of the two Teichmüller lifts of ω_{f′}^{a′^(0)_i}. Here ω_{f′} uses geometric Artin reciprocity; its inverse is used when importing the arithmetic Artin convention. This refines the existing mod-p τ(s,μ+η), and is not a second definition of that mod-p type.
hypotheses: p is prime; K/Q_p is unramified of degree f≥1, q=p^f; E/Q_p is finite and sufficiently large; O=O_E has uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field F.
σ_j=σ_0∘Frob_p^j indexes embeddings cyclically; cyclotomic Hodge–Tate weight is +1; no determinant is fixed.
proofSteps: Use the tame quotient and local reciprocity to obtain the fundamental characters, with the geometric/arithmetic inverse made explicit.
Form the two integer exponents and Teichmüller lifts; Frobenius permutes them, so the sum extends to a Weil representation with open inertia kernel.
Reduction of each Teichmüller character recovers the MP.3 tame-character formula.

nodes.title: Eigenbasis Frobenius matrices
nodes.statement: Let M be rank two in the imported Y^[0,h],τ(R), with eigenbasis β for a fixed 1-deep lowest-alcove presentation (s,μ). Put K′/K unramified of degree r, L′=K′((−p)^{1/e′}), v=(u′)^{e′}, E(u′)=v+p. Decompose S_{L′,R}=(W(k′)⊗_{Z_p}R)[[u′]] by σ_{−j′}, so φ sends M^(j′) to M^(j′+1). Define C by β^(j′+1)C^(j′)=φ_M(φ*β^(j′)). Define A^(j′)=Ad((ṡ′_{or,j′+1})⁻¹(u′)^{−a′^(j′+1)})(C^(j′)). The order of the two conjugations is part of the definition. Then A belongs to M₂(R[[v]]), is upper triangular modulo v, and is f-periodic. On O-flat p-complete R, the imported Hodge-bound subfunctor Y^≤λ,τ is tested by divisibility of i-minors by (v+p)^{Σ of the smallest i entries of λ_j}.

Conjugate in the stated order. The descent-character exponents force v-integrality; orientation forces the lower-left entry to vanish modulo v.

For any tame inertial type τ, the twisted JH set meets W(ρ̄) iff τ≅τ_{w̃} for some w̃∈Adm∨. Thus X(σ)={w̃:∀j,w̃_j≠θ(σ)_j} has cardinal 2^f, and τ_{w̃}, w̃∈X(σ), are pairwise distinct. If σ=F(t_{μ−η}(sω)), then θ(σ)_j=U₃ when ω_{f−1−j}=0 and U₁ when that coordinate is η.

nodes.title: Polynomial gauge charts
nodes.statement:
For each embedding table index j put z=v+p. Each local ambient ring R_j is O[[eight variables]], with the two starred coefficients equal to their fixed nonzero residual Teichmüller values plus formal variables; every other displayed coefficient is a formal variable. Define the three matrices
A₁=[[z²e₁₁*+zd₁₁+c₁₁,c₁₂],[v(zd₂₁+c₂₁),zd₂₂*+c₂₂]],
A₂=[[zd₁₁+c₁₁,zd₁₂*+c₁₂],[v(zd₂₁*+c₂₁),zd₂₂+c₂₂]],
A₃=[[zd₁₁*+c₁₁,zd₁₂+c₁₂],[vc₂₁,z²e₂₂*+zd₂₂+c₂₂]].
The matrices are at embedding f−1−j. The constants a₁,a₂,a₃∈Z_(p) are the actual oriented exponent differences divided by e′ in the monodromy computation; modulo p they are respectively −sgn(s_j)(r_j+1)+1, sgn(s_j)(r_j+1)+1, −sgn(s_j)(r_j+1)−1. They depend on the whole type. All displayed denominators are units under section4 hypotheses.
For A₁ set u=e₁₁*, d=d₂₂*, a=a₁, x=c₁₂d₂₁/(ud). Its ordered polynomial equations G₁,…,G₅ are
(d₁₁+(a−2)c₁₂d₂₁/d,
 c₂₂−(a−1)c₁₂d₂₁/u,
 c₂₁+(a−1)(a−2)c₁₂d₂₁²/(aud),
 c₁₁−(c₁₂d₂₁/d)((a−1)²(a−2)x/a−p),
 c₁₂((a−1)(a−2)x−2p)).
For A₂ set u=d₁₂*, d=d₂₁*, a=a₂, t=d₁₁d₂₂/(ud). The list is
(c₂₁+(a−1)d(t+p),
 c₁₂−au(t+p),
 c₁₁+a(a−1)d₁₁(t+p)/(a+1),
 c₂₂−a(a−1)d₂₂(t+p)/(a−2),
 (t+p)(a(a−1)t/((a−2)(a+1))+p)).
For A₃ set u=d₁₁*, d=e₂₂*, a=a₃, x=d₁₂c₂₁/(ud). The list is
(d₂₂−(a+1)d₁₂c₂₁/u,
 c₁₁+ad₁₂c₂₁/d,
 c₁₂−a(a+1)d₁₂²c₂₁/((a−1)ud),
 c₂₂−(d₁₂c₂₁/u)(a²(a+1)x/(a−1)−p),
 c₂₁(a(a+1)x−2p)).
Let I^poly_j be the ideal of these five equations. Its two polynomial component ideals P^poly_{j,21}, P^poly_{j,30} are I^poly_j plus, respectively, the first and second factor of G₅. Fractions mean multiplication by the indicated units. In each chart the dense polynomial subring uses c₁₂/e₁₁*,d₂₁/d₂₂* in chart 1; d₁₁/d₁₂*,d₂₂/d₂₁* in chart 2; and d₁₂/d₁₁*,c₂₁/e₂₂* in chart 3, with the remaining coordinates unchanged. It is a polynomial algebra in eight parameters. Let R=⊗̂_O R_j and I^poly=Σ_j I^poly_j R.

σ_j=σ_0∘Frob_p^j indexes embeddings cyclically; cyclotomic Hodge–Tate weight is +1; no determinant is fixed.
ρ̄:G_K→GL₂(F) is semisimple. Fix (s,μ) with ρ̄|_{I_K}≅τ(s,μ), s_j=1 except s₀=w exactly in the irreducible case.

A type w̃ and a semisimple residual gauge module from T.4 are fixed. The two residual unit values may vary with j.
proofSteps: Apply the rank-two gauge degree bounds to obtain A₁,A₂,A₃ and exactly eight independent scalar parameters per embedding.
Expand det A−(its leading unit)z³ to obtain the three finite-height coefficient equations; use the h=3 leading monodromy jets for the eight monodromy equations.

Use p-saturation and elimination in the actual reduced O-flat quotient to deduce G_i∈(I∞,p^{N−5}), where I∞ denotes the actual finite-height and monodromy closure. These five equations define the polynomial model, not yet the actual ideal.

nodes.title: Irreducible crossing equations
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete DVR, A=O[[x₁,…,x_n]], n≥2, d>0, and u∈A×. Then x₁x₂+ϖ^d u is irreducible and generates a prime ideal. That ideal differs from (x₁). If u₁ and u₂ have different residues in A/m_A, their associated principal ideals differ. This is a sufficient residue test, not an equivalence for all u₁,u₂.
hypotheses: O is any complete DVR here; the section4 prime and genericity bounds are unnecessary.
proofSteps: Replace x₂ by x₁+x₂ and apply the pinned Weierstrass preparation/division theorem in x₁ over O[[x₂,…,x_n]]. Any proper factor forces a root b in that coefficient ring’s maximal ideal.
The equation b²+bx₂+ϖ^d u(b,…)=0 implies ϖ^d divides b or b+x₂, since x₂ is not divisible by ϖ. Dividing gives a contradiction to u being a unit.
The imported regular-local UFD theorem makes irreducible elements prime. Compare Weierstrass factors and constant coefficients to distinguish the indicated ideals.
acceptance: The unit hypothesis excludes x₁x₂+ϖx₁, which is reducible.
Ramified O is allowed: p is a positive uniformizer power times a unit, so the lemma applies to xy+up.

nodes.title: Effective Jacobian bound
nodes.statement: For each dense eight-variable chart with ideal (G₁,…,G₅), let J₅ be the ideal of the 5×5 minors of its Jacobian matrix. Then p³∈I^poly_j+J₅; in charts 1 and 3 even p² lies in that ideal. For chart 2 put x=d₁₁/d₁₂*,y=d₂₂/d₂₁*, b=(a₂−2)(a₂+1)/(a₂(a₂−1)), F=b⁻¹(xy+p)(xy+bp). Eliminating G₁,…,G₄ identifies the relevant minors with F_x,F_y. The identity (2(b+1)xy+p(b−1)²)F−((b+1)xy+p(b²+1))xF_x=p³(b−1)² proves the assertion, since b and b−1 are units.

Verify the displayed polynomial identity after multiplying by b to clear its unit denominator. Since p>2 and a₂,a₂−1 are units, b−1=−2/(a₂(a₂−1)) is a unit.

All denominators are units using the stated N-deep inequalities.

nodes.title: Effective chart approximation
nodes.statement: Let A be a p-adically complete Noetherian p-torsion-free O-algebra. For one of the three normalized chart systems G in eight variables and an approximate point a∈A⁸ in its fixed residual chart, suppose G(a)∈p^n A⁵ and n>6. There is an exact point a° with G(a°)=0 and a°−a∈p^{n−3}A⁸. Consequently, for n=N−5 the actual reduced O-flat chart A=R/I∞ receives an O-map R/I^poly→A congruent to the natural coordinate map modulo p^{N−8}; it is a surjection for N≥12. This is the specific chart consequence of Elkik’s lemma, rather than a new plan for arbitrary henselian approximation.
hypotheses: p is prime; K/Q_p is unramified of degree f≥1, q=p^f; E/Q_p is finite and sufficiently large; O=O_E has uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field F.
σ_j=σ_0∘Frob_p^j indexes embeddings cyclically; cyclotomic Hodge–Tate weight is +1; no determinant is fixed.

proofSteps: Evaluate the Jacobian bound: p³ belongs to the evaluated Jacobian-minor ideal, since G(a) is divisible by p^n and 1−p^{n−3}c is a unit. Adjugate matrices give a right inverse to the Jacobian after division by p³.

Correct the approximate point by an element in p^{n−3}A⁸. Taylor expansion raises the error exponent to 2(n−3)>n. The Jacobian bound persists because the correction is divisible by p⁴. Iterate; p-completeness gives a zero with the asserted precision.

Apply this to every j in the actual quotient, where model accuracy gives n=N−5≥7. Tensor the maps, extend continuously to the completed tensor product, and use identity on the relative cotangent space to get surjectivity.
acceptance: At N=12, n=7>6 and the coordinate correction is p⁴.
At n=6 the stated iteration need not improve the error; it is deliberately excluded.
A singularity bound alone does not identify the quotient: T.5/nonempty-profiles and component counting are still required.

The input lifting-existence contract is the R08.3 request: the GHLS extended-Fontaine–Laffaille seed and the compact-type constituent criterion, translated to cyclotomic weight +1 as used by BHHMS equation (26). nodes.title: Effective ambient comparison
nodes.statement: Let I∞⊂R be the kernel of the maximal reduced O-flat quotient of the finite-height and actual monodromy equations for the fixed gauged residual module. The approximation map R/I^poly→R/I∞ is an isomorphism. It lifts to an O-algebra automorphism ψ:R≅R with ψ≡id mod p^{N−8} and ψ(I^poly)=I∞. Define I_j=ψ(I^poly_jR) and P_{j,λ}=ψ(P^poly_{j,λ}R) using this one ψ for the entire type. Then I∞=ΣI_j and Σ_jP_{j,λ_{f−1−j}} are exactly its distinct minimal primes. Although I^poly_j lies in R_j, I_j and P_{j,λ} generally do not: their tails involve all embeddings.

The imported completed-tensor component theorem gives 2^f components of relative dimension 3f for R/I^poly. The actual generic ring has the same dimension and at least 2^f components from nonempty-profiles and the imported fixed-type dimension theorem.
The surjection cannot lose or shrink any component: its kernel is contained in all the model’s minimal primes, whose intersection is zero.

Lift the quotient isomorphism by ψ(X_i)=X_i+p^{N−8}ε_i. Its invertible linear term and complete local power-series evaluation give an ambient automorphism. Transport every factor and equation by the same ψ.
acceptance: The congruence is modulo p^{N−8}, hence at least p⁴ in the stated range.
Do not independently choose a small perturbation for each factor or each embedding.

nodes.statement: For each exact profile λ, R_{ρ̄}^{λ,τ_{w̃}}/ϖ is reduced and every irreducible component is formally smooth over F. Apply the substitutions to the full coupled series of each type, with its constants a_i; do not substitute in independent one-embedding approximations. proposedRoadmaps.brief:
Final theorems (Böckle–Iyengar–Paškūnas, Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023) e30), for every finite F/Q_p, every d ≥ 1 and every continuous ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, L large enough: (1) Theorem 1.1 — R^□_ρ̄ is a local complete intersection, flat over O, of relative dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p], and R^□_ρ̄/ϖ is a complete intersection of dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p]; so every ρ̄ lifts to characteristic zero, and absolutely irreducibly (Corollaries 3.45, 3.61). (2) Theorem 1.2 — R_{det ρ̄} → R^□_ρ̄ is flat and induces bijections on irreducible components and on π_0 of the generic fibres; the components are the Spec R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ for χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×, and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ are normal domains and complete intersections. (3) Corollary 1.3 — R^□_ρ̄ is reduced and R^□_ρ̄[1/p] is normal. (4) Theorem 1.4 — for ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ are factorial except when d = 2, F = Q_3 and ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄(1), where they are not; Corollary 4.23 gives factoriality for d = 2, [F:Q_p] ≥ 4 and d ≥ 3, [F:Q_p] ≥ 3. (5) Theorem 1.5 — for ψ lifting det ρ̄, R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄/ϖ are normal domains and complete intersections of dimensions dim R^□_ρ̄ − dim R_{det ρ̄} + 1 and dim R^□_ρ̄ − dim R_{det ρ̄}, and R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ is O-flat. (6) Proposition 1.12 — absolutely irreducible points are dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p] and Kummer-irreducible points in Spec R^□_ρ̄/ϖ. Also the same complete-intersection statements at every closed point of X^gen and for representations over local fields (Corollaries 3.38, 3.44), for A^gen, A^{gen,χ}, A^{gen,ψ} (Corollaries 3.40, 4.6, 5.8, Proposition 4.26), and the consequences for R^ps (Corollaries 4.27–4.29, 5.10–5.11, Lemma 4.30).

proposedRoadmaps.brief: Build on Local Galois deformation rings and their components (LocalGaloisDeformationRings), whose L7 constructs Kisin's rank-n potentially semistable lifting rings of fixed labelled Hodge type, their characteristic-zero points and dimension, and whose L8 separates ordinary conditions. This Part II owns §2 of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne, 'The Ramanujan and Sato–Tate conjectures for Bianchi modular forms' (Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025) e10). Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 2.5.5 (Theorem D): if p > d, K/ℚ_p is finite and E/ℚ_p contains the Galois closure of K, then for every ρ̄ : G_K → GL_d(𝔽) the special fibre R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄}/ϖ of the weight-0 crystalline lifting ring (Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1, …, d − 1} at every embedding) is generically reduced.
